title: Componentwise restriction Hom isomorphisms natural in coefficient complex
statement: For a scheme Y, open U and cochain complex L of Y-modules, there exists a family of chain isomorphisms between the restriction of Hom(L,M) and Hom(restrict L, restrict M), indexed by M, whose hom components are natural in every chain map M ⟶ N.

source.place: Lemma 20.42.3, ordinary Hom restriction and postcomposition compatibility

proof.text: Construct the natural internal-Hom comparison for Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι from lem-sc-internal-hom-restrict-scheme. Restriction preserves integer-indexed products: reflect limits through the forgetful functor to presheaves for the over-U restriction, compose with the over-open equivalence, and transfer preservation along overFunctorEquiv U. Additivity follows from the restriction adjunction.

Choose the product projections specified by homComplex_projections_exists on Y and U. In each degree and for each coefficient complex, use the source and target product universal properties and the factorwise internal-Hom isomorphisms to construct mutually inverse maps. Record their projection equations for arbitrary p+n=q.

Postcompose the two candidate differential composites with every target product projection. Expand both signed Hom differentials using homComplex_projections_exists. Additivity of restriction preserves the two summands and the integer-unit sign; the two-variable naturality of the factor comparisons identifies their pre- and post-composition terms. Product extensionality proves differential compatibility, and isoOfComponents assembles the degreewise isomorphisms.

For a coefficient chain map, use HomologicalComplex.hom_ext and the target product universal property. The projection specification identifies the Hom functor map as postcomposition in each factor. The projection equations for the constructed isomorphisms and naturality of the internal-Hom comparison identify the two composites. Thus the chosen chain isomorphisms are natural in the coefficient complex.

proof_origin.description: B3: direct product construction over scheme module sheaves, including signed differential compatibility and coefficient naturality. The existing projection interface is named by a private proposition, re-expressed over an abstract site by a proved private conversion lemma, and used with explicit category and functor parameters inside the original theorem. This prevents repeated conversion of the concrete restriction and chosen Hom functor. Uses a proved sheaf-level transport lemma; does not use the objectwise open-restriction theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem homComplex_restrict_scheme_natural_components {Y : Scheme.{u}} (U : Y.Opens)
    (L : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℤ) :
∃ e : ∀ M : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℤ,
      ((homComplexFunctor (R := Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf)).obj (op L) ⋙
          (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj M ≅
      ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        (homComplexFunctor (R := U.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf)).obj
          (op (((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj L))).obj M
    , ∀ {M N} (f : M ⟶ N),
      ((homComplexFunctor (R := Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf)).obj (op L) ⋙
          (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map f ≫ (e N).hom =
      (e M).hom ≫ ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        (homComplexFunctor (R := U.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf)).obj
          (op (((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj L))).map
          f
